Hierarchical (agglomerative) clustering of a data matrix

Source: R/clustering.R
hclust_fun.Rd

A thin, deterministic wrapper around stats::hclust() + stats::cutree() that cuts an agglomerative hierarchical clustering into k groups. It is a pure function of x (no randomness, no global RNG use), which makes it a valid black-box clustering routine to pass to selective_hotelling_bc() (the package's preferred, exact selective test for arbitrary clustering algorithms).

By default the tree is built on squared Euclidean distances (stats::dist(x)^2), matching the clusterpval / KmeansInference selective-conditioning convention; set square = FALSE for ordinary Euclidean distances.

Unlike kmeans_fun(), the returned object deliberately carries no init_centers_idx field: hierarchical clustering has no random initialization to condition on, so it should be treated as a pure black box and never re-seeded.

Usage

hclust_fun(x, k = 3, method = "average", square = TRUE)

Arguments

x

A numeric \(n \times p\) data matrix with observations in rows.

k

Number of clusters to cut the dendrogram into.

method

Agglomeration method passed to stats::hclust() (e.g. "average", "single", "complete", "ward.D2").

square

If TRUE (default) the dendrogram is built on squared Euclidean distances (stats::dist(x)^2, the clusterpval convention); if FALSE, ordinary Euclidean distances (stats::dist(x)) are used.

Value

A list with elements:

cluster

An integer vector of length nrow(x) of cluster labels in 1:k (from stats::cutree()).

trajectory

A length-1 list, list(cluster). Hierarchical clustering has no Lloyd iterations, so the "trajectory" is a single (final) assignment vector.

The object intentionally does not include an init_centers_idx field.

Details

Hierarchical clustering helper for selective inference

See also

selective_hotelling_bc(), selective_hotelling_test()

Examples

set.seed(1)
X <- matrix(rnorm(30 * 2), 30, 2)
cl <- hclust_fun(X, k = 3)$cluster
table(cl)
#> cl
#>  1  2  3 
#> 27  1  2
